transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Damien Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (VerdantTech Procurement), Liam O'Neal (VerdantTech Legal), Priya Rao (VerdantTech InfoSec), Daniel Park (VerdantTech CTO)

Summary (auto): procurement review of MSA/DPA, SLA selection, pricing and onboarding steps.

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. we'll do a quick run through the redlines, SLA options, and any final pricing questions. Damien and I will handle the technical and benchmark items.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Hi, thanks. we have Liam and Priya on the line — they're the ones looking at the legal and security pieces. Daniel's here in case of infra questions.
[00:20] Liam O'Neal: Quick note — we'll focus on a few DPA clauses (data subject rights, subprocessors), and some SLA language around credits and remedies.
[00:29] Damien Cole: Great — from a tech standpoint we also want to confirm the expected throughput, token sizes, and whether you'll need VPC/on-prem.
[00:36] Priya Rao: We do need VPC peering; customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement. also SOC2 report and ISO 27001 cert if you have it.
[00:45] Ava Martinez: Understood. Redwood supports customer KMS integrations (KMS/HSM), and we can provide SOC 2 Type II and our security pack — I'll attach those. on ISO, we are in progress — Damien correct me if I'm wrong.
[00:55] Damien Cole: We're in progress on ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II is available. small transcription hiccup from the recorder — it shows "Redwood Dedicate" sometimes, meant 'Redwood Dedicated'.
[01:05] Maya Singh: On the MSA we've proposed a couple of redlines around indemnity and limitation of liability. do you have standard language for regulated customers?
[01:14] Ava Martinez: We have an enterprise MSA template for healthcare/finance customers; happy to map your redlines into that. typically limitation of liability is negotiable with a tiered cap tied to fees.
[01:23] Liam O'Neal: For DPA, we want specific subprocessors listed or a commitment to notify 30 days prior to changes. also audit rights — can Redwood support quarterly audits?
[01:34] Damien Cole: Audit logs and per-request tracing are available via Redwood Console; for quarterly audits we'll coordinate with our security team — might be covered under our SOC 2 reporting plus targeted support. i'll put that in the action items.
[01:46] Daniel Park: On the infra side, we plan to run a couple of heavy-latency flows during our POC — 8k token summarization and an embeddings job. what's the performance delta between hosted and dedicated?
[01:57] Damien Cole: Good question. Hosted is great for quick start, but for predictable latency and throughput the Dedicated pools are better — you get reserved GPUs and consistent KV cache behavior. we typically see in our benchmarks a 20-40% latency improvement for steady-state workloads on Dedicated versus general hosted endpoints, depending on model and quantization.
[02:12] Maya Singh: Pricing — procurement needs clarity. you sent a quote for a monthly commit (Reserved) and the pay-as-you-go numbers. what's the practical cutoff where Reserved makes sense?
[02:22] Ava Martinez: For most customers doing steady inference, once you're above about 5M tokens/month or doing predictable batch inference, Reserved capacity lowers per-token costs substantially. the pricing sheet we sent has three tiers: Starter commit, Growth, and Enterprise — Growth tends to be best for teams with stable traffic.
[02:36] Liam O'Neal: And the SLA credits — how are they calculated? we want clarity on remedies.
[02:41] Ava Martinez: SLA credits are percentage-based credits off monthly fees, with escalation and an uptime target. For Dedicated there's an SLA with both uptime and tail-latency SLOs. we can send the exact table; in previous redlines we've accepted a two-tier remedy ladder and cap tied to monthly fees.
[02:58] Priya Rao: For KMS, can Redwood support JIT rotation, and can keys live in our tenant KMS (Azure Key Vault)?
[03:06] Damien Cole: Yes — we support Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS integrations; JIT rotation workflows can be integrated, but we'll need the engineering window. also note, for Private deployments we can do customer-managed HSM if you need air-gapped certs.
[03:20] Maya Singh: Data residency — we need logs and data to stay in the EU. is that supported?
[03:25] Ava Martinez: Yes, we offer region pinning; we can route your traffic to EU-hosted capacity and ensure logs are stored in-region. we'll include that in the DPA.
[03:34] Liam O'Neal: About subprocessors — instead of a static list, we want notice and an opt-out window for material changes.
[03:41] Ava Martinez: We usually provide a current list and a 30-day notice for changes; opt-out for material changes is something we can discuss with Legal.
[03:50] Daniel Park: Benchmarks — Damien, what do you need from us to run a POC benchmark?
[03:55] Damien Cole: We'll need sample prompts, average token lengths, concurrency targets, and a test window with expected QPS. ideally a small dataset we can use to replicate your workload. we'll run both dedicated and hosted runs and share latency/throughput and cost delta.
[04:12] Maya Singh: Timeline — procurement wants approvals by mid-July. if we get the redlined MSA back quickly, can you accomodate that?
[04:20] Ava Martinez: Yes — if we have the redlines by 7/9, legal and contracts can turn around in 2-3 business days typically. finance will need to approve the pricing; we can feed them the final quote.
[04:31] Liam O'Neal: There was a small point on the DPA about deletion of logs — we need a 90 day retention by default and ability to purge on request.
[04:39] Damien Cole: Console supports retention controls; we'll set default to 90 days and provide purge APIs for manual removal.
[04:46] Priya Rao: Does Redwood provide attestations for penetration tests or can we run one?
[04:52] Ava Martinez: Customers typically get our SOC 2 and we can coordinate a point-in-time pentest for Dedicated/Private with appropriate scope. we'll need to align on an NDA if you want vendor-run tests.
[05:04] Maya Singh: On support — what is the SLA for P1 incidents and response times?
[05:09] Ava Martinez: Enterprise customers with Dedicated capacity get 24/7 on-call and a 1-hour response for P1s plus escalation paths. Support package details in the addendum.
[05:19] Liam O'Neal: One last legal: can you add a clause for escrow or source access in extreme cases?
[05:25] Ava Martinez: For enterprise deals we can discuss code escrow for critical components; it's uncommon but possible as part of an extended enterprise contract. we'll note it for legal.
[05:34] Daniel Park: Any blockers from infra? we need to ensure VPC setup and peering doesn't take more than two weeks.
[05:40] Damien Cole: VPC peering is typically 3-10 business days once networking details are provided; we'll prioritize you and coordinate with your cloud team.
[05:48] Maya Singh: OK, let's recap next steps.
[05:51] Ava Martinez: Recap: Redwood sends merged MSA/DPA with comments (Ava), Redwood SE schedules benchmarks with provided sample (Damien), VerdantTech provides KMS and data residency requirements (Priya), VerdantTech legal provides final signoff criteria (Liam). Target dates noted in action items.
[06:05] Liam O'Neal: Thanks everyone. we'll aim to get redlines back by Friday.
[06:08] Ava Martinez: Great — talk soon.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and auto-transcription swapped a few product names; speakers repeated a phrase mid-utterance a couple times.

References/shared artifacts mentioned: pricing-quote-verdanttech-2026-06-30.pdf (sent prior), security-pack-soc2.zip (will be shared), benchmark-plan-template.xlsx (SE to share).
